harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a 3-node MariaDB 10.11.19 Galera cluster (galera-4 provider) across node1/node2/node3 on RHEL 7.9. Deployed galera.cnf with wsrep_cluster_address=gcomm://node1,node2,node3 and mariabackup SST; bootstrapped node1, joined node2/node3 via SST, all reached Synced/Primary state. Verified multi-master write propagation across all three nodes, demonstrated availability during a one-node outage (quorum preserved on 2/3), and confirmed automatic IST resync when the stopped node rejoined. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id + cluster health baseline on each node, restarted node1, node2, and node3 sequentially via systemctl reboot, confirmed each boot_id changed, and verified MariaDB auto-started and each node rejoined the cluster as Synced/Primary with all data intact after every restart.
actions_performed: Inspected all 3 RHEL 7.9 nodes; found no active RHEL subscription repos but internet access
Added archived MariaDB 10.11 rhel7-amd64 yum repo (yum.mariadb.org redirects to mirror) on all nodes
Enabled rhel-7-server-optional-rpms/extras-rpms and installed archived EPEL7 repo to resolve dependencies (pv, pcre2, perl modules)
Installed MariaDB-server, MariaDB-client, galera-4, MariaDB-backup on all 3 nodes
Opened firewalld ports 3306/4567(tcp+udp)/4568/4444 on all nodes
Populated /etc/hosts with CLUSTER_HOSTS and set up cluster SSH key for node-to-node file transfer
Generated SST and root passwords on node1 via openssl rand; copied secret files to node2/node3 over SSH without ever printing them; never placed literal credentials in any command
Wrote /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf per node with wsrep_cluster_address, wsrep_node_address/name, wsrep_sst_method=mariabackup, wsrep_sst_auth (via command substitution from the secret file)
Bootstrapped node1 with galera_new_cluster, created sst db user, set root password, configured ~/.my.cnf per node for password-based access
Started mariadb on node2 then node3 sequentially; each joined via SST reaching wsrep_cluster_size 3 / Synced
Enabled mariadb service on boot on all nodes
Created clustertest.pings table and wrote rows from node1, node2, node3, verifying each write appeared on all other nodes

Stopped node3, confirmed cluster stayed available (size 2) and accepted writes from node1 and node2, then restarted node3 and confirmed automatic IST resync (log evidence: 'IST received', 'synced with group') and full data presence

Captured per-node boot_id + wsrep health baseline, then restarted node1, node2, node3 one at a time via systemctl reboot; polled each until exec access returned, confirmed boot_id changed on all three, and verified MariaDB auto-started with cluster_size 3 / Synced / Primary and all 5 test rows intact after each restart

evidence.requirement: Writes through any member are available from the other members (multi-master replication)
evidence.summary: Inserted rows from node1, node2, and node3 into clustertest.pings and confirmed each write appeared on all other nodes' SELECT output.

evidence.requirement: Database stays available when one member is unavailable (quorum preserved)
evidence.summary: Stopped mariadb on node3; cluster reported wsrep_cluster_size=2 on node1 and both node1 and node2 accepted new writes while node3 was down.

evidence.requirement: Unavailable member resynchronizes automatically when it returns
evidence.summary: Restarted mariadb on node3; it rejoined at wsrep_cluster_size=3/Synced, its SELECT showed both rows written while it was down, and journalctl logs show explicit IST completion ('IST received', 'synced with group').

evidence.requirement: Cluster fully configured with 3 members (topology/setup)
evidence.summary: node1 bootstrapped as a 1-node cluster; node2 and node3 sequentially joined via SST reaching wsrep_cluster_size 2 then 3, all Synced.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline captured
evidence.summary: Captured node1 boot_id (e9250ad1...) plus wsrep_cluster_size=3/Synced and pings COUNT=5 before restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnect, boot identity changed, and post-restart recovery proven
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged asynchronously; node became unreachable then returned with boot_id beeecdda... (changed from baseline); mariadb auto-started, rejoined as Synced with cluster_size 3 and COUNT=5 intact.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline captured
evidence.summary: Captured node2 boot_id (151c4aa9...) plus wsrep_cluster_size=3/Synced and pings COUNT=5 before restart.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnect, boot identity changed, and post-restart recovery proven
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged asynchronously; node became unreachable then returned with boot_id 46960e08... (changed from baseline); mariadb auto-started, rejoined as Synced with cluster_size 3 and COUNT=5 intact.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline captured
evidence.summary: Captured node3 boot_id (a8e7c48c...) plus wsrep_cluster_size=3/Synced and pings COUNT=5 before restart (post-earlier resync test).

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnect, boot identity changed, and post-restart recovery proven
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged asynchronously; node became unreachable then returned with boot_id 8fb947e2... (changed from baseline); mariadb auto-started, rejoined as Synced with cluster_size 3 and COUNT=5 intact.

evidence.requirement: Final full-cluster health and data consistency after all three restarts
evidence.summary: node1 shows wsrep_cluster_size=3, cluster_status=Primary, all three incoming addresses present, and all 5 test rows consistent across the cluster.
